answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identity to thermoelectric proof-of-work. Nodes continuously sign transactions using energy harvested from thermal gradients in porous basalt, a greenhouse garden, or arctic tundra. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated Seebeck generators and acquiring land for each clone. However, seasonal shifts that equalize ambient temperatures can temporarily starve honest nodes of operating energy.
